name: Heartside Hill
award: 2022 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Heartside Hill is a 71-apartment affordable community (one to four bedrooms, 30% to 60% of AMI) by CARE Housing on land donated by Heart of the Rockies Christian Church at Lemay Avenue and Trilby Road in south Fort Collins, part of a campus with Habitat for Humanity homes, L'Arche homes and a community building; it won $1,171,431 a year in federal 4% credit and $989,961 in state credit in CHFA's 2022 Round Two and opened in August 2025.
why_it_matters: It is a working example of church-donated land turned into a mixed campus (rentals, for-sale homes, homes for adults with disabilities and an early childhood center), with 16 project-based vouchers and Zero Energy Ready construction, and it won a national AHTCC award in 2026.

status.label: Open: opened 2025-08-07 and leasing
status.detail: Denver7 reported that Heartside Hill officially opened on Thursday 2025-08-07, and CARE Communities' site says the apartments are open and accepting applications. No dated construction-start or placed-in-service record was found.

next_step: Look for CHFA records of the placed-in-service year and 8609s, and the City of Fort Collins permit and certificate of occupancy history.

key_numbers.meaning: 5 at 30% AMI, 8 at 40%, 8 at 50% and 50 at 60%; 36 of 71 have three or four bedrooms.

From Housing Catalyst, on the 30%, 40% and some 50% AMI units.

background.text: The church chose three nonprofits to receive the land; the property was conveyed to Community at Heart LLC and CARE holds a purchase option for the apartment parcel.

The Fort Collins Planning and Zoning Commission unanimously approved the overall development plan after nearly three hours of debate; neighbors' input led CARE to put the apartments on the south side next to existing multifamily housing and the single-family homes on the north.

Expansive bentonite clay required 30-foot drilled piers (about $200,000 more per building) and deep over-excavation of drive lanes; the application requested a basis limit waiver and cut almost $4M through redesign.
The application expected vertical construction to start in June 2023 after building permits.
In October 2026 CARE reported a national award from the Affordable Housing Tax Credit Coalition in the Resilient and Healthy Housing category.
No asterisk footnote applies to this row in the award report; its asterisks only key the Type and Target codes.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award report and application count 71 apartments, while Denver7 reported 72 affordable rental units at opening.
The award report lists $16,100,000 of bonds, while the application described $16,550,000 of construction bonds.
The application says the donated property is 8.84 acres, while the planning approval coverage describes a site of just under 11 acres.
